observed_symptoms.fact: A configuration change in Atlanta started the outage; Atlanta attracted traffic from across the backbone until 21:39.
Traffic dropped about 50% across the network. Impact was localized to locations connected to the backbone.

Nineteen locations were named as affected, including San Jose, Dallas, Seattle, Los Angeles, Chicago, Washington DC, Richmond, Newark, Atlanta, London, Amsterdam, Frankfurt, Paris, Stockholm, Moscow, St. Petersburg, Sao Paulo, Curitiba and Porto Alegre; other locations were normal.
Internal traffic manager showed Atlanta CPU at overload while affected locations' CPU dropped to near zero because they handled no traffic.
After recovery, congestion at a core data center that processes logs and metrics dropped some logs until 22:10; the edge continued operating normally.

confirmed_root_cause.mechanism: While responding to backbone congestion (loss of the Newark-Chicago link at 20:25), engineers meant to remove Atlanta routes from the backbone. A one-line change instead deactivated the prefix-list inside the 6-SITE-LOCAL term of the 6-BBONE-OUT policy rather than deactivating the term. The term then accepted all BGP routes, tagged with local-preference 200. Local routes from compute nodes had local-preference 100 and local-preference is transitive in iBGP, so all backbone traffic for local compute went to Atlanta compute nodes and overwhelmed the Atlanta router.
confirmed_elements: Trigger was a configuration edit on the Atlanta router
The correct change would have been to deactivate the term instead of the prefix-list
contributing_factors: A prior backbone link failure had created congestion that prompted the change
No maximum-prefix limit on backbone BGP sessions

investigation_evidence.evidence: Router config comparison showed the prefix-list under the 6-SITE-LOCAL term marked inactive.
The full term set local-preference 200, added communities, and accepted routes matching the prefix-list.
Traffic manager tool showed Atlanta CPU overloaded and affected data centers' CPU near zero; unaffected data centers unchanged.

recovery_actions.action: Disabled the Atlanta router, dropping it from the backbone.
recovery_actions.why: Stop it attracting traffic; the network is built to work without a backbone.

recovery_actions.action: Changed BGP local-preference for local server routes (deployed after the incident) and planned a maximum-prefix limit on backbone BGP sessions (July 20).
recovery_actions.why: Prevent a single location from attracting other locations' traffic.

recovery_verification.method: Traffic began flowing normally once the Atlanta router was disabled.
Atlanta fully dropped from the backbone; service restored.
Full recovery including logs and metrics.

acceptable_alternatives.description: Disable or isolate the Atlanta router
Correct the Atlanta policy by deactivating the term instead of the prefix-list
acceptable_alternatives.basis: Source names this as the correct pre-incident change but does not say it was applied during recovery

acceptable_alternatives.description: Lower local-preference on local server routes; add maximum-prefix limits
